The *Jīvika Sutta* ("Lifestyle", Iti 91) is a canonical discourse situated in the third section of the *Itivuttaka* (It 3.42, PTS It 89) [SuttaCentral]. In this sutta, the Buddha examines the reasons why thoughtful individuals undertake the alms-seeking religious life, while highlighting the moral and spiritual dangers that confront practitioners if they neglect mental training [SuttaCentral].
Full parallels are preserved in the Chinese Buddhist canon as MĀ 140 (至邊) and T 765.94 (苦), alongside resembling parallels found in the *Piṇḍolya Sutta* (SN 22.80) and SĀ 272 [SuttaCentral]. Computational analysis by DharmaNexus aligns segments §3.1–3.2 with the Sanskrit *Udānavarga de Subaši* (best score 95) [DharmaNexus]. Internally within the Pali canon, DharmaNexus records 110 shared passages across 16 texts, notably matching prose descriptions with the *Mahāsāropama Sutta* (MN 29), the *Cūḷasāropama Sutta* (MN 30), AN 4, AN 3, MN 67, and SN 22 [DharmaNexus].
